domain_restrictions: A is a nonzero polynomial with integer coefficients
B is a nonzero polynomial with integer coefficients
A divided by B is assumed to be a polynomial in Z[q], not merely a rational function
Degree is interpreted only for nonzero polynomials
semantic_sketch_json.normalized_claim: For every pair of nonzero integer-coefficient polynomials A and B, if the quotient A divided by B is again an integer-coefficient polynomial, then the degree of A is greater than or equal to the degree of B.
quantifier_order: For all polynomials A and B in Z[q], if A and B are nonzero and A divided by B is a polynomial in Z[q], then deg(A) is at least deg(B).
witness_dependencies: The conclusion depends only on the given polynomials A and B

statement_nl: Let A(q) and B(q) be nonzero polynomials in Z[q]. If the rational function A(q) / B(q) is itself a polynomial in Z[q], then deg(A) >= deg(B).
